transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-06-12 15:00 PDT - duration ~52m. Attendees: Jane Miller (Redwood AE), Ravi Kapoor (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Sarah Chen (Luminary CTO), Miguel Torres (Luminary ML Eng), Priya Reddy (Luminary SecOps), Tom Baxter (Luminary Product)

Summary: Discovery focused on model selection for a mix of multilingual, tool-calling, and long-context chat use cases. Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Wants benchmarks on open models (Llama-family, Mistral, Falcon variants) for 8k/32k/64k contexts and function/tool calling reliability. Security and KMS questions flagged for Private.

00:00:05 Jane Miller: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jane from Redwood, i'll do quick agenda - product + infra options, model selection tradeoffs, then Ravi will do tech Qs, and we'll capture next steps.
00:00:18 Sarah Chen: Hey thanks, quick note, we're on Pacific time too, so appreciate it.
00:00:25 Ravi Kapoor: Great - just to set context, Luminary is building multilingual customer support & doc-assistant flows with occasional tool calls to internal APIs, is that right Sarah?
00:00:33 Sarah Chen: Yep. Main constraints: high-quality answers in English and Spanish, occasional Mandarin, need up to 32k context for long documents, and tool-calling reliability is critical for actions like ticket creation. We want low latency for web UI, cost matters but we err on reliability.
00:00:52 Miguel Torres: Also we do some batch embedding work but primary is generation/chat. We'll consider embeddings separately.
00:01:02 Jane Miller: Perfect. A couple notes: Hosted is fastest to start, Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput, Private (VPC/on-prem) is for strict data residency and KMS control.
00:01:18 Tom Baxter: On dedicated, do we still get the same model catalog as hosted? Any feature differences?
00:01:26 Lena Ortiz: Mostly same catalog; some larger context variants may be limited by infra but we can surface compatible variants. There is also a routing policy so requests can fallback to a smaller variant if Dedicated capacity is constrained.
00:01:41 Priya Reddy: Security questions up front: SOC 2 status, audit logs retention, SSO/SAML, and KMS/HSM integrations. For Private, we need HSM option.
00:01:54 Jane Miller: We're SOC 2 - i'll send the pack. We support SAML SSO and RBAC; KMS/HSM integrations available on Private, and Dedicated can integrate KMS for keys too.
00:02:10 Sarah Chen: On models - we're evaluating open models to avoid vendor lock. Which models should we start with for multilingual + tool calling?
00:02:19 Ravi Kapoor: Common open choices: Llama 3 variants (if permitted), Mistral Mix, Falcon 180B variants, and a few newer community-optimized models. For multilingual, some Llama-family models have good pan-lingual ability, but Mistral sometimes outperforms on instruction-following in EU languages. Falcon is strong for long-context when tuned.
00:02:39 Miguel Torres: What about context length? We need 32k for doc ingestion - do we need special kernels or is it just model variant?
00:02:47 Ravi Kapoor: A bit of both. Model architecture and tokenizer matter; some variants are trained for 32k or 64k contexts. On the runtime side, our serving runtime picks kernels and manages KV cache - we sometimes hit memory/latency tradeoffs at 64k. For 32k we usually recommend Dedicated with x reserved capacity or Private if you want control.
00:03:08 Jane Miller: Practically, we run a benchmark: same prompt set at 8k/32k to measure latency and token cost. We'll include quantized variants (8-bit/4-bit) so you can see cost vs quality.
00:03:20 Sarah Chen: Tool-calling - we need deterministic function call success >99%. Any caveats with streaming responses + function calls?
00:03:29 Lena Ortiz: Tool-calling reliability usually depends on how you handle retries and idempotency. We support structured tool-calling with streaming; sometimes tokenizer chunking can split the function call payload on very long contexts, so we put checks and fallbacks in the SDK. We'll show examples.
00:03:47 Miguel Torres: Do the open models support the same function-calling primitives as the big hosted APIs? We rely on structured JSON outputs.
00:03:55 Ravi Kapoor: We provide SDK-level wrappers that normalize function-calling semantics across models. Some community models require prompt shaping or a small output-parser shim, but our SDK handles most of that. Expect some model-specific prompt engineering.
00:04:12 Priya Reddy: Data residency - if documents contain PII, can we keep embeddings and KV cache off Redwood-hosted persistent storage?
00:04:21 Jane Miller: Yes, Dedicated and Private give options. Hosted has configurable retention and you can opt-out of storing inputs. For Private you control all storage. We'll include the exact retention settings in the security pack.
00:04:34 Tom Baxter: Competitor question - how is this different from going OpenAI with function-calling and then home-brewing the rest?
00:04:42 Jane Miller: The difference is predictable economics and operational tooling: batching, KV caching, routing, and dedicated pools. We also provide model quantization recommendations and A/B rollouts for model versions. Plus easier private deployments for regulated environments.
00:04:58 Miguel Torres: Latency numbers - can we get p95 token latency for 4-bit quantized Mistral-70B at 8k and 32k?
00:05:06 Ravi Kapoor: We'll put numbers in the benchmark sheet. Ballpark: on Dedicated we might see p95 around 120-200ms per token at 8k with aggressive batching; at 32k it increases and memory pressure adds higher tail latency. Exacts depend on instance type and batch config.
00:05:26 Sarah Chen: For our UI, p95 < 600ms end-to-end per response ideally. Is that realistic with 32k context?
00:05:34 Ravi Kapoor: For short responses with relevant cached prefixes, yes. For full 32k doc syntheses, end-to-end will be higher - we can architect using summarized shards and on-demand full-doc runs.
00:05:46 Miguel Torres: Any recommendations for multilingual tokenization issues, like Chinese tokenization giving huge token counts?
00:05:52 Lena Ortiz: We recommend model-specific tokenization analysis; sometimes you get inflated token counts - we can provide tools to estimate tokenization across languages and suggest model variants that handle CJK better.
00:06:05 Tom Baxter: About cost: is Dedicated billed by reserved GPU hours? Do you have burst capacity?
00:06:12 Jane Miller: Dedicated has monthly commits but configurable autoscaling policies and a burst pool for spikes. We'll include sample pricing scenarios based on expected QPS and token volumes.
00:06:24 Priya Reddy: On Private deployment - how heavy is the on-prem package? Do we need specific GPU fleets and networking setups?
00:06:30 Ravi Kapoor: For on-prem, we provide a package that expects a k8s cluster with GPUs, recommended driver and CUDA versions; we have an air-gapped installer and optional control-plane connectivity. We can share the ops guide.
00:06:44 Miguel Torres: For the benchmark, we'll share 150 representative prompts - some short, some 25k-token docs. Is that enough?
00:06:51 Jane Miller: That's perfect. We'll run at least Llama-3 variant (if licensing ok), Mistral Mix 70B, Falcon-180B compat, and a trimmed community 32k model. We'll include quantized runs.
00:07:04 Sarah Chen: Licensing note - we need to confirm which Llama variants are permissible for commercial use.
00:07:09 Jane Miller: Good point - we'll add a licensing note per model in the benchmark doc; legal will advise on Llama 3 commercial terms.
00:07:18 Tom Baxter: How long for the pilot? We were thinking a 2-week PoC with benchmarks and small Dedicated commit during that window.
00:07:25 Jane Miller: Two weeks is standard for benchmarks. We can spin up a limited Dedicated pool for benchmarking or run hosted with priority routing.
00:07:33 Priya Reddy: Can we get a copy of the audit logs format - we need to ingest to our SIEM.
00:07:38 Lena Ortiz: We'll share sample audit logs and retention options; they can be exported to your S3 or pushed to SIEM.
00:07:46 Miguel Torres: Any gotchas on embeddings when using quantized models? We need stable vector representations for similarity search.
00:07:53 Ravi Kapoor: Embeddings are sensitive to quantization; we typically recommend dedicated embedding models or using unquantized variants for embeddings. We'll include an embedding quality comparison in the benchmark.
00:08:05 Sarah Chen: For monitoring, we need token-level cost, latency breakdowns, and per-route dashboards.
00:08:12 Jane Miller: Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-model dashboards, tracing hooks, and error analysis. We'll demo that in the follow-up.
00:08:23 Miguel Torres: About tool-calling reliability again - can we get example code for function-calling with retries and idempotency patterns?
00:08:30 Ravi Kapoor: Yes we'll attach SDK snippets and a small sample service that shows robust retries, idempotency token handling, and streaming + function-call integration.
00:08:40 Tom Baxter: Any reference customers doing similar multilingual + tool-calling flows?
00:08:45 Jane Miller: We can share anonymized case studies - a few customers in fintech and SaaS do similar. I'll include references.
00:08:52 Sarah Chen: Great. Can you also show us cost tradeoffs of more aggressive caching/prefixing vs raw model calls?
00:08:59 Lena Ortiz: We'll include caching scenarios in the Optimize recommendations - caching prefixes and KV cache can reduce per-token calls significantly for repeated dialogs.
00:09:10 Miguel Torres: Ok let's recap next steps.
00:09:14 Jane Miller: Recap: 1) We'll send pricing + benchmark template (Jane). 2) SEs will run benchmark on requested models/contexts and deliver p95 numbers and embeddings quality (Ravi/Lena). 3) Luminary to share sample prompts, dataset and security questionnaire (Miguel/Priya). 4) Schedule Private deployment deep dive if needed (Jane).
00:09:33 Sarah Chen: Sounds good. Thanks all.
00:09:36 Jane Miller: Thanks, we'll follow up with links: benchmark spreadsheet, security pack (SOC2, KMS), sample SDK snippets and audit log example.
00:09:46 Miguel Torres: Thanks. End call.

Notes: Transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "KV cash" vs KV cache), and proper nouns may be imperfect. References shared: benchmark spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/luminary-template), security pack (link: https://redwood.example.com/security/luminary-pack), SDK snippets repo (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples).
